시편-10-1.title: 시편 10장 1절 역사문법적 주해
시편-10-1.exegesis: 20. By their effectual subjection, make them to realize their frail nature ( Psa 8:4 ), and deter them from all conceit and future rebellion.
시편-10-1.theologicalNote: 20. By their effectual subjection, make them to realize their frail nature ( Psa 8:4 ), and deter them from all conceit and future rebellion.

시편-10-2.title: 시편 10장 2절 역사문법적 주해
시편-10-2.exegesis: PSALM 10 Psa 10:1-18 . The Psalmist mourns God's apparent indifference to his troubles, which are aggravated by the successful malice, blasphemy, pride, deceit, and profanity of the wicked. On the just and discriminating providence of God he relies for the destruction of their false security, and the defense of the needy. 1. These are, of course, figurative terms (compare Psa 7:6 ; 13:1 , &c.). hidest-- Supply "thine eyes" or "face."

시편-10-3.title: 시편 10장 3절 역사문법적 주해
시편-10-3.exegesis: 2. Literally, "In pride of the wicked they (the poor or humble, Psa 10:17 ; 12:5 ) shall be taken in the devices they (the proud) have imagined."
시편-10-3.theologicalNote: 2. Literally, "In pride of the wicked they (the poor or humble, Psa 10:17 ; 12:5 ) shall be taken in the devices they (the proud) have imagined."

시편-10-4.title: 시편 10장 4절 역사문법적 주해
시편-10-4.exegesis: 3. heart's-- or, "soul's." desire-- that is, his success in evil. and blesseth, &c.-- he (the wicked) blesseth the covetous, he despiseth the Lord.
시편-10-4.theologicalNote: 3. heart's-- or, "soul's." desire-- that is, his success in evil. and blesseth, &c.-- he (the wicked) blesseth the covetous, he despiseth the Lord.

시편-10-5.title: 시편 10장 5절 역사문법적 주해
시편-10-5.exegesis: 4. The face expresses the self-conceit, whose fruit is practical atheism ( Psa 14:1 ).
시편-10-5.theologicalNote: 4. The face expresses the self-conceit, whose fruit is practical atheism ( Psa 14:1 ).

시편-10-6.title: 시편 10장 6절 역사문법적 주해
시편-10-6.exegesis: 5-6. Such is his confidence in the permanence of his way or course of life, that he disregards God's providential government (out of sight, because he will not look, Is 26:11 ), sneers at his enemies, and boasts perpetual freedom from evil.

시편-10-8.title: 시편 10장 8절 역사문법적 주해
시편-10-8.exegesis: 7-10. The malignity and deceit ( Psa 140:3 ) of such are followed by acts combining cunning, fraud, and violence (compare Pr 1:11 , 18 ), aptly illustrated by the habits of the lion, and of hunters taking their prey. "Poor," in Psa 10:8 , 10, 14 , represents a word peculiar to this Psalm, meaning the sad or sorrowful; in Psa 10:9 , as usual, it means the pious or meek sufferer.

시편-10-12.exegesis: 11. As before, such conduct implies disbelief or disregard of God's government.

시편-10-13.title: 시편 10장 13절 역사문법적 주해
시편-10-13.exegesis: 12. (Compare Psa 9:19 ; 3:7 ). the humble-- (Compare Psa 10:17 , and Margin.) lift up thine hand-- exert thy power.
시편-10-13.theologicalNote: 12. (Compare Psa 9:19 ; 3:7 ). the humble-- (Compare Psa 10:17 , and Margin.) lift up thine hand-- exert thy power.

시편-10-14.title: 시편 10장 14절 역사문법적 주해
시편-10-14.exegesis: 13-14. It is in vain to suppose God will overlook sin, however forbearing; for He carefully examines or beholds all wickedness, and will mark it by His providential (Thine hand) punishment.
시편-10-14.theologicalNote: 13-14. It is in vain to suppose God will overlook sin, however forbearing; for He carefully examines or beholds all wickedness, and will mark it by His providential (Thine hand) punishment.

시편-10-16.title: 시편 10장 16절 역사문법적 주해
시편-10-16.exegesis: 15. arm-- power. till thou find none-- So far from not requiting ( Psa 10:11 , 13 ), God will utterly destroy the wicked and his deeds ( Psa 9:5 , 6 ; 34:16 ; 37:36 ).
시편-10-16.theologicalNote: 15. arm-- power. till thou find none-- So far from not requiting ( Psa 10:11 , 13 ), God will utterly destroy the wicked and his deeds ( Psa 9:5 , 6 ; 34:16 ; 37:36 ).

시편-10-17.title: 시편 10장 17절 역사문법적 주해
시편-10-17.exegesis: 16-18. God reigns. The wicked, if for a time successful, shall be cut off. He hears and confirms the hearts of His suffering people ( Psa 112:7 ), executes justice for the feeble, and represses the pride and violence of conceited, though frail, men (compare Psa 9:16 ).
